name: Process: Design what the house does with the mentor relationship after the plan
text_content:
P32, answering carryovers 86akhb2wj and 86akhpvhj's mentor half. After the plan the house records only the shape the person stated in the career conversation block (S9 I7) and takes no further act, because a recorded standing relationship is a line about two people. Where the person states "continue," the stack may treat overlap with the former mentor as a scheduling preference of the person's, honored where the schedule allows, never required, and written on no one's page. The mentor never becomes a sponsor or an advocate ("The system is the advocate", WP p.11), a coach, a channel for the lead, or a person the lead asks about the former mentee; the relationship reproduces through the pool, where the former mentee becomes eligible once their own plan has closed with its goal held. Recognition of mentoring beyond shift stays Session 13's. Extends 86akhb2q3 and 86akhb2r8 by reference. Normal.

name: Founder decision: Ratify the playground test as six questions, the ten employee conditions, and their verdicts
text_content:
P3, P4, P6, and P45. Canon's one-line test ("does this build or foreclose conditions for agency?", Canon 1.0, section 01) is run on a mechanism as six questions: the condition, the legible rule, the open-ended result, the tight edge, the loose edge, and the documented reason with the diagnostic read that would notice the condition's absence; the two edges are Deck 3.0's own ("Rules so tight the result is foreclosed"; "Openness so loose the space stops feeling safe", p.14). "Conditions for agency" for an employee decomposes into ten: legible rules, a stated range, judgment built not procedure only, safety to err, safety to speak, being known, a path, time that is not taken, a say in the rules, and a place of their own. Each is tested against a mechanism and given one of three verdicts: four are mechanisms (legible rules, a stated range, safety to err, a path), five partial (judgment, safety to speak, being known, time not taken, a say in the rules), and one slogan today (a place of their own); belonging among the team is read as the outcome the conditions produce, not a condition. The non-negotiables outrank the philosophy on every verdict, which is Deck 3.0's order and is marked held under 86akh3rx4. Blocks I5, row 129, and every environment item below. High.

name: Process: Run the repeat reads: a domain, a seat, a period, and a designation held every service
text_content:
P18, P19, and P32. At the partners' review on the recurrence, a domain that repeats is read in three questions (the count, the sheet, the lead's load) before any hiring question, and a domain producing departures is read as cooling failure first. A seat opened by tension loss twice in a year is a sheet question (horizon, shift shape, physical demands, range), never the person who left. A period whose incidents cluster in one class has the variety pass re-run; a period whose dependent interfaces go empty in practice goes to the gate review as a separate restaurant. A designation held by one person every service for a quarter is, at the reset, a question about the Maitre d's seat's hours and the designation's rule in three branches (the schedule or a rotation floor; the eligible pool widened by forms; a rotation floor against preference), never a second seat, and the holder's performance is never read from the count. name: Process: Design the departure read in three passes, and what the brief carries
text_content:
P30, answering carryover 86akh7r0c's departure half. The week of a departure: the inventory's tension-loss row (field 15, what the node held), the leads' review's line naming what the node held and which seats carry it, the pool read recorded before the seat opens externally, and the adjacent seats' thermal-load and check-in lines over the following weeks. Then the memory-failure read the record's five modes do not carry by name (finding 19.1): whether what the node held was in the system, with each "in its head" written as sequence corruption or skill invisibility, so the departure's cost is bounded in the only unit this program carries, which mechanism now has to be maintained. Then, at re-fill, whether the re-established node carries the tension, as a read-back. The floor hears the structural fact as coverage at the brief under its standing change line and nothing about the person; this reconciles S3 P11.6 (told at the brief with its tension map) with S7 P47 (nothing about a person is said to the floor) and S8 P49 (no announcement) by narrowing the tension map to coverage, and the practice is Session 11's. Blocks I8 and row 113. High.

name: Process: Design the path from a diagnosis to a versioned change and its read-back
text_content:
P24, P25, and P26. A diagnosis produces care or correction: a process update from a capture is care, logged against the capture with an owner and never versioned; a change to a mechanism's rhythm, spine, range, trigger, or rule, to a designation's rule, to a seat, a line, or a period is correction and is versioned on the mechanism map, the inventory, the goal page, or the sheet. Four paths: a mechanism through the leads' review and the reset; a designation's rule through a structure change entry; a seat through Session 8's path whole (S8 P49); a line or a period through the variety pass at a gate. The evidence line is the change's reason field, verbatim, and a change with no line or with a person as its reason is refused. Every change carries the mode and object it was made to clear and is read back on the next scorecard by the source that raised it, as cleared, not cleared, or cannot read; a change not cleared on two lines goes to the reset, which decides whether the mechanism or the mode was wrong before naming a second fix. What changes at the reset only and what may change between resets is listed on the page. Extends 86akhcz3c and 86akh676p by reference. Blocks row 110 and I4. High.

name: Process: Run the pre-opening first run of the diagnostic before dinner's gate
text_content:

name: Process: Run the diagnostic inside dinner's first-quarter freeze, with the held list
text_content:
P21. Inside the freeze the diagnostic reads everything (closes, briefs, check-ins, the leads' review, the pulse, the pipeline read, the infrastructure line) and changes nothing on the room's mechanism map. It may make shift-close maintenance from a capture and log it as care, set a parameter inside a range the leads' review already holds, version a build-side document, and name a designation differently at the next brief; it may not change the check-in's interval, the brief's spine or block, a range's width, a trigger's destination, a designation's rule, the leads' review's day, or the close's fields. Every line raised in the quarter that would change a frozen mechanism goes to the partners' page marked held for the first reset with its date, so the first reset opens on a list. A seat opened by tension loss is recruiting, not the room's cadence, and proceeds. Extends 86akh672x by reference. Blocks row 112. Normal.

name: Process: Design how a structure change is made and reaches the team
text_content:

A structure change (creating or retiring a seat, changing a line, adding a period's seats or designations, changing a designation rule or an inventory mark) is a versioned entry on the inventory on the partners' page with its reason written first in the record's terms, proposed by the domain lead through the leads' review and versioned by the partners' review. name: Build the stack's person-side recruiting records: the training record, the person page's entries, the ready-now pool, and the consent record

Per specifications I19, I21, I23, and I24. name: Build the scorecard set, the packet, and the practical's pay record
text_content:
Type: instrument

Per specifications I8 through I14. The phone screen scorecard reads must-haves and availability only. The first-interview scorecard records evidence against each of the four reads the stage assesses, the candidate's own words on what they need from the building, and a decision with the read named. The practical's scoring form records the station, the service and whether the leads' review flagged it, whether the practical ran with load or without, who worked beside the candidate, procedure mastery and reproduction under load marked against the sheet's entry-level procedures, the candidate's treatment of the steward, the runner, and the trainer, and the hours told against the hours worked. The practical's pay record pays every practical through Rippling, including a cancelled or shortened one, under the employment form W6 closes. The dinner-in-the-room scorecard, and the pre-opening substitute's, is submitted independently by each partner after the meal and never at the table. The founder-stage scorecard reads the non-negotiables and the fourth read only, and a no that names no read is not a no. The packet refuses a decision while any scorecard is missing and refuses a hire while any scorecard carries a non-negotiable flag. Across the whole set: no free-text verdict, no column for presence or charm or how the room felt, no weighting or numeric composite, independent submission before interviewers speak, and no scorecard travelling to a person page. Five instruments are refused outright and must not be built by habit: her work style grid, the résumé review and the take-home, the hiring committee and the hiring meeting, her recruiter's interview loop, and the bias-neutralizing copy tool (I26 to I30). Gated on the document methodology, W19, W6 for the pay record, and W1 for kitchen rubrics.

name: Name cross-period fluency as a development marker
text_content:
Type: structure

The record names one development marker, cross-strand fluency, makes it visible in the web as more connections, and recognizes it in compensation as meaningful. Everything else in the record requires a second one: one restaurant and one brand met at different times of day, late night as dinner's own later register, one system and four moods, same foundation and four registers, each period continuing the one before it. All of that asks the same person to hold a different register at a different hour, and the record names no marker for it and says nothing about whether it is recognized (finding 15.1, P62). It bears on recruiting because one labor pool staffs the periods, the seat sheet's service-period field is where a second period is recorded, and the first period expansion is the first succession event, so the dinner cohort is being hired into a fluency the record has not named. The structural element to finalize: cross-period fluency named as a development marker parallel to cross-strand fluency and recorded on the person page as connections. Whether it is recognized in compensation is Session 13's; its structural placement is Session 8's; both receive it as carryovers.

name: Render the web as a designed organizational artifact
text_content:
Type: structure

The transparency sheet's first item is "the org chart," and Part I of the record spends its length arguing that the org chart is the load-bearing misread; the artifact the record wants instead is one of its own open items, the web rendered as a designed organizational artifact rather than a chart (finding 15.2, P32, I6). This is the first thing a candidate reads, at the first interview, before any offer, and a lead candidate reading a box above their seat will arrive with exactly the playbook the lead rubric is built to refuse. What the render must show: the candidate's node, its adjacent nodes by seat, its domain lead by seat, the two leads and the center as the record describes them, parallel and neither above the other, and the record's own words for the structure. What it must refuse: a vertical line from the candidate's node to anything, a box, a title implying altitude, "reports to," and any whole-house chart that places the candidate at the bottom of something. It is re-rendered per seat, not once for the house. Until it exists, the field carries the record's words and the candidate's neighborhood drawn by hand, and the render is not a gate on the first interview. The owner sits under the record's visual design open item and the founders name it; this item does not decide that.

name: Add recruiting's parameters and the founder stage to the mechanism reset
text_content:
Type: process

Session 4 placed the mechanism reset after dinner's first quarter, after the first full year, then annually, reading every mechanism against its record, cost, and buy. Recruiting hands it four things. The founder stage: pre-opening it is the last scored stage for every seat, and the team's recommendation for the reset is that it ends for edge seats and continues for lead seats permanently, since the leads are the center's peers and their dinner in the room already has the partners at the table; the reset ratifies that against the stage's own record (P53, P54, I13). The response window is a parameter of the reset and not a law (P29). The candidate pulse's monthly reads feed it (I16). And every recruiting instrument names the reset as its revision rhythm, so the reset is where the seat sheet, the scorecards, the answer set, the pool tag, the referral record, the pipeline read, and the decision-rights entries are re-read (section 14). The process to design is what recruiting's section of the reset agenda contains and what evidence each line opens on.

name: Sequence the kitchen chain and carry its state on the partners' page
text_content:
Type: process

Under either branch of the chef ruling, the kitchen pipeline runs in a fixed chain with no link skippable: the ruling, then the chef in the seat, then canon's Session 1B and the culinary philosophy, then the menu, then the kitchen's seat sheets, then kitchen practicals, then kitchen hires, then their training, then dinner's gate (P58, section 10.3). Until the chef is seated and the menu exists there is nothing for a kitchen practical to reproduce, so no kitchen practical can run and the kitchen's readiness cannot be tested at all. The process to design: the chain as a dated record on the partners' page, each link carrying a date or the row fails at that link, read at every gate review, with the hiring timeline built against it rather than against the opening date (readiness row 59). The kitchen's station, plate, mise standard, and rubric are the chef partner's and are chef-gated (P44). The hiring timeline itself is Session 6's and receives this as a carryover.

name: Place recruiting's reads on the leads' review and the partners' domain read
text_content:
Type: process

Recruiting carries three standing reads and none of them has a placement yet. The pipeline read is one standing line at the weekly leads' review, carrying per open seat the stage counts, the candidates past window, the source mix, and the seat's age; the team recommends it be read under the load reading, since an open seat is a load on adjacent nodes, and it enters either under one of Session 4's eight agenda items or as a ninth line (P28, I22, S4 P26). Behind it the stack surfaces continuously and without anyone asking: any candidate outside the four states, any candidate past the response window with no dated action, any seat open past three consecutive leads' reviews, sent to the domain lead and the Maitre d. A seat past three reviews goes to the partners' review as a possible node-overload entry. The house response window is five days from any stage's completion to a sent decision, shortenable on a sheet and never lengthenable (P29). The candidate pulse's single open question travels with every decision, hire or decline, and is read monthly at the partners' domain read by the Maitre d, for the process and never for the person, anonymized (P30, I16). The source-dominance and stage-rate read runs at the leads' review with no target and no figure (P26). Readiness rows 42 and 58 check the placements. No candidate's name appears in the leads' review record.

name: Write the candidate into the content approval framework
text_content:
Type: document

The content approval framework routes green-light, strategic review, and leadership review, and has no class for a person who is not team, may never be, and is named nowhere in it; meanwhile the documented build names a chef search as material and its method invites the audience into real decisions (finding 15.4). The gap sits exactly where the record most wants to publish. Session 5's answer adds one rule rather than a new class: any content that would identify a person as a candidate is leadership review and requires a consent record dated after the decision before it moves; everything else about a search is green-light, including the seat, the process, the founders' reasoning, and the house's own performance against its response window (P18, P19). The document states what the build may never show without that consent (any candidate's identity, image, voice, application, or scorecard; any content from a phone screen, interview, practical, or dinner in the room; any reference to a specific person as a candidate) and what it may never do at all (invite the audience to weigh in on a candidate, stream or film an assessment stage, use a search's setbacks as content while a candidate is in process). Owner: Brandon's seat as the brand cadence's owner. The consent record itself is built under W24 (I19); readiness row 53 checks both.

name: Rule whether the house states a position on the composition of its team
text_content:
Type: founder decision

The record holds inclusion mechanics and no position on who the team is: interview language choice protects dignity, the fourth read asks what the building must supply for this person, engagement is measured across psychological safety and values alignment, and nothing states a goal or a read on the composition of the team (finding 15.6). Her chapter treats referral-driven homogeneity as first-order and her workbook scores a recruiter on it, and each of the record's own four sources narrows: the founders' reach, the referral, and a build audience that self-selects. The team does not assert a position for the house. It recommends the read that any position would need regardless: Greenhouse's source and stage data read at the leads' review for whether any single source dominates a seat's pipeline and whether any stage declines a group of candidates at a rate the others do not, with no target set and no figure (P26, I22). Without a position, that read can report and cannot act. Routed to Session 11, whose subject is inclusion, and returns to the founders from there. Does not block the cohort.

name: Rule the chef seat, and with it which branch of third-seat recruitment runs
text_content:
Type: founder decision

The record disagrees with itself. The white paper holds the chef as "an equal founding partner" with an equal vote on whether a service period is built; both canon versions hold the seat as "[HELD], Pending Executive Chef Hire" with two named hiring criteria, the Mahk standard and the chef's relationship to Bangjja Yugi, Baekja, Buncheong, and Cheongja (page section 10.3, finding 15.7, P57). Session 5 argued both branches to the ceiling and did not pick. Branch A, partner: not recruiting at all, but a partnership negotiation belonging with the operating agreement, canon's criteria as the founders' due diligence rather than a scorecard, a cooking for the founders in a kitchen the candidate chooses as the last round, and three terms settled in writing (that the culinary identity is the brand's and the dishes are the chef's; that the chef partner's vote on a service period is equal and their vote on brand canon is not; that the seat sits in a code-bearing organization). Branch B, hire: the leadership process in full, canon's criteria as field 8 of the chef's seat sheet, a cooking as the paid practical, and two record artifacts rewritten (the lunch decision as an equal decision among all three partners, and the record's account of the founders). Under either branch the kitchen pipeline is gated in a fixed chain and the culinary identity is the brand's (P58). The kitchen practical's station, plate, mise standard, and rubric wait on the seated chef (P44, chef-gated). This is first in the order because the hiring timeline places the chef first, every kitchen row, sheet, and entry waits on it, and readiness row 59 holds dinner's gate closed until the ruling is filed. The ruling is already open as founder decision 86akh2qrp, to be filed at 86akh3tw9; this item is the recruitment design that turns on it.

name: Split every seam-crossing metric at the domain boundary
text_content:
Type: process

Source: Session 3 of the Scaling People translation program, page section 9.3 of the S3 page in the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253. Session task 86ajgmhgx.

No metric has two owners. A metric that crosses the seam between the two parallel leads is split into a stack-side measure owned by the Operations Lead (the record travels; the profile is one across periods; the invisible advocate's mechanics run) and a floor-side measure owned by the Maitre d (recognition delivered; the customer was invited across; the team's health). Where a metric cannot be split, its owner is the daypart charter's "held by" entry.

name: Operate the cross-domain and lead-to-lead escalation rules
text_content:
Type: process

Source: Session 3 of the Scaling People translation program, page section 4.3 of the S3 page in the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253. Session task 86ajgmhgx.

Class B: the owning domain decides; any affected domain is consulted before the event; an unresolved objection holds the decision and escalates to the founder whose domain holds the disputed outcome, or to both partners if it belongs to both. Class C: a disagreement between the two parallel leads escalates the same way, experience to Brandon's seat, cost to Dominic's, both to the partners. Class D: emergency authority and closure as specified. Class E: no stack change that alters what a lead or server does during service lands without the affected domain consulted through the feedback channel.

name: Run the alert-actor rule
text_content:
Type: process

Source: Session 3 of the Scaling People translation program, page section 10.7 of the S3 page in the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253. Session task 86ajgmhgx.

For every automated alert the stack can raise, a person is named in advance to act on it, with their range on receipt and the path by which they report cause and fix. The named actor is never a founder by default; an alert that routes to a founder is a design fault. Alerts route to the domain owner whose outcome they touch. No alert is enabled without an entry in the alert register.

name: Draw the transparency line
text_content:
Type: founder decision

Source: Session 3 of the Scaling People translation program, page sections 8.4 and 11.2 of the S3 page in the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253. Session task 86ajgmhgx.

name: Rule whether the operating system is built for three service periods or four
text_content:
Type: founder decision

Source: Session 3 of the Scaling People translation program, page section 13.2 of the S3 page in the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253. Session task 86ajgmhgx.

Both canon versions state four dayparts at the address and specify lunch fully, with nothing marked held. The white paper states a core of three, with lunch and brunch "held in reserve, not part of the core and not assumed," subject to an equal three-partner decision that may remove lunch entirely. On status this is a disagreement, not an altitude difference. The operating system resolves its own dependency by running whatever set of periods holds a ratified daypart charter. The founders rule whether canon's four-daypart statement is a design readiness or a decision, and whether canon is versioned to mark lunch as held. Routed to the canon reconciliation Session 2 filed.

custom_fields.value: I met Chris and his wife, in Pullman Market. After talking with them about the market for a bit, they asked if the company was looking for investors. name: Instrument: The held-and-deferred register format for the charter (gated on `86ajgn2z5`)
text_content:
Canon already runs a held-and-deferred structure in its "What remains" section. The charter needs the same discipline, tightened.

Must contain: every held statement names who closes it, meaning founder, chef partner, or team; every deferred statement names the condition that opens it rather than a date.

What it is for: it is the chef partner's inheritance on day one, the honest account of what the two seated founders did not close on the third seat's behalf. It is also the charter's check against a settled-looking answer to an open question, which the white paper names as the tell of a document that has not been pressure-tested.

Gated on the document methodology, ClickUp task 86ajgn2z5. This item specifies the instrument. It does not build it.

Filed by Session 2. Specification is in section 12 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Instrument: The founding seat description template (gated on `86ajgn2z5`)
text_content:
The instrument that answers the carryover on founder job descriptions (86ajgnhp7): neither founder has one, and the chef partner cannot be told what they own until the other two seats are written down.

Eight elements per seat: domain owned; outcomes the seat is accountable to; decisions held alone; decisions shared; what the seat does not own; the seams with the other seats; relationship to the two parallel leads and to the operating system; the absence rule, meaning what happens in the domain when the seat is not in the building.

Must refuse: interior qualities, strengths, failure modes, and working style. Those belong to each founder's own writing, and to Session 16. The seat description is the outward half only.

Gated on the document methodology, ClickUp task 86ajgn2z5. This item specifies the instrument. It does not build it.

name: Instrument: The daypart charter template (gated on `86ajgn2z5`)
text_content:
One page per service period. This is Sŏn's replacement for her team charter, which does not map: her unit is a team inside a division inside a company, and Sŏn has strands, domains, two parallel leads, and four service periods rather than divisions.

Must contain: reason to exist; what it becomes; first customer; what it is measured by, leading indicators only; what it gives the connective layer; what makes it a worse version of dinner; what it hands on to the next period; what it draws from the previous one; operating logic; held by.

Must refuse: code names for service periods, revenue targets, any figure, and any content that reads as a description of dinner.

It is also the form the lunch decision takes. The record holds that whether lunch is built at all is an equal three-partner decision and a real option to remove. A lunch charter that cannot be written without describing a worse dinner is the record's "no good answer for lunch," arrived at structurally rather than by opinion.

Gated on the document methodology, ClickUp task 86ajgn2z5. This item specifies the instrument. It does not build it.

Filed by Session 2. Specification is in sections 11.3 and 12 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Structure: Sharpen the founder deadlock question with the interim two-partner case and the reserved decision classes
text_content:
Extends founder decision 86akh2qht, which asks how three equal partners break a deadlock. Session 2 adds two parts that decision did not carry.

The interim case. Until the chef partner is seated there are two partners, and two equal votes have no majority. An interim deadlock rule is needed now, not when the third seat fills. Every founder decision filed by Sessions 1 and 2 runs through it.

The reserved classes. Which decisions are reserved to all partners rather than owned in a domain. Candidates drawn from the record: building or removing a service period (the record already treats lunch this way); changing a non-negotiable; versioning the charter; versioning canon at tiers 1 or 2; admitting a new principal.

Depends on the operating agreement report (86akh3t62), which may already settle voting among principals.

Requires Dominic. Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in section 8.2 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Structure: Rule on the chef seat as partner or hire and reconcile the two accounts
text_content:
Extends founder decision 86akh2qrp, which Session 1 filed as a disagreement about who owns culinary identity. Session 2 read both documents in full and found the disagreement runs deeper: the two artifacts may not be describing the same seat.

The white paper says "chef partner": an equal founding partner who "owns the culinary vision" (WP p. 03), freed from carrying the rest of the business (WP p. 05), with an equal vote on whether lunch is built at all (WP p. 36).

The canon says "Executive Chef": a hire, gated by criteria the brand sets. "Mahk standard is an explicit hiring criterion." Held items sit under "pending Executive Chef hire." The relationship to Bangjja Yugi, Baekja, Buncheong and Cheongja is "a hiring criterion." Above it sits the architecture-tier non-negotiable that "culinary identity belongs to the brand, not the chef."

A hiring criterion is an instrument applied to a candidate. It cannot be applied to a founding partner on the same terms.

The ruling decides: the seat's standing in charter and canon versioning; its place in decision rights and in deadlock; whether it sits in the operating agreement or in the point system; and whether Sessions 5 and 6 design the recruitment of a principal or the hiring of an executive.

Requires Dominic. Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in section 9 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Process: Write every decision-rights instance in the operating system in owner, range, triggers form
text_content:
The record assigns decision rights at least eight times and never states the rule: lunch as an equal three-partner decision; sonic governance in three named tiers; floor authority split between server and floor manager; the David protocol as a system decision and never a floor call; the design system governed by one owner with an RFC path; naming requiring three-party sign-off; content at green-light, strategic review, and leadership review; and the server's authorized generosity range.

They share one shape. Authority sits with the closest competent owner. The range within which that owner acts without asking is stated in advance. The triggers that escalate are named before the event rather than judged during it.

Session 3 adopts this as the form for every decision-rights entry in the operating system, rewrites the eight existing instances into it, and treats an entry missing any of the three parts as incomplete.

Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in section 8 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Process: Schedule the principles revision after dinner's first quarter and after the first full year
text_content:
The charter's principles are drawn from decisions because Sŏn has no operating history. Her drafting method, writing down notable moments in the company's history and asking what belief prevailed, becomes available only after the company operates.

Version one of the principles is therefore marked pre-opening, and a mandatory revision is scheduled at two points: after dinner has run alone for its first quarter, which the record sets as the phased opening's first gate, and after the first full year.

Session 4 places this on the operating cadence. Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in section 6.3 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Document: Write the operating charter
text_content:
Sŏn's founding document, specified section by section in Session 2 of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

Sections: standing; mission; long-term commitments; non-negotiables; protection order; principles; founding seats; decision rights; people and compensation commitments; one company across the day; structure; refusals; held and deferred; versioning.

Seven design rules: commitments and owners, never tools or addresses; every statement is settled, held, or deferred; versioned by decision; written under Sŏn's voice rules and passing canon's six binary tests; no figures; never assert the unproven; cites canon rather than restating it.

The charter is a debt the record already incurred rather than an import from the book: the white paper commits onboarding to orientation on "the mission, the values, and the behavioral standard" before operational training (WP p. 20), and stakes the company on not depending on "either founder's memory" (WP p. 06). Neither is satisfiable while the mission and values exist only in the founders' heads.

Depends on the founder decisions filed alongside this item. Sections whose inputs are not yet ruled are written as held rather than guessed.

Filed by Session 2.

name: Document: Reconcile the two canon artifacts into one version of record
text_content:
sources/brand-guidelines.md (Version 1.0) and sources/brand-guidelines-deck.pdf (Version 3.0) have drifted from each other on the six-tier authority hierarchy, on the presence of "the order is the decision," and on the chef seat's terminology. Canon's own rule is that a living document "changes by versioned decision, never by drift," so the drift is a violation of canon by canon.

The work: name one artifact the canon of record and the other a rendering of it; apply the tier ruling from 86akh3rx4; scope the authority claim "the source of truth for every decision made under this name" to what canon actually governs; and state canon's relationship to the operating charter in the same words the charter uses.

Follows the hierarchy ruling. Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in sections 3 and 4 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Founder decision: Select and word the long-term commitments and the principles
text_content:
The record holds candidates for both and has never sorted them.

Long-term commitment candidates: the three compounding engines (organization, customer, brand); the leading indicators the white paper commits to (employee NPS, cultural labor score, customer recognition rate); a company "built to run without them" (WP p. 06); coherence across the day, each service period with its own reason to exist. None carries a figure, which is what makes them well formed.

Principle candidates, stated in the record as mechanics: authority lives in the domain; the first question is what allowed this, not who failed; management absorbs blame from staff; if it matters to the experience, Sŏn pays for it; there is no hierarchy of importance; never assert the unproven; advancement requires preparation, not permission; employees are the users.

Brandon selects which are long-term commitments, which are principles, and which are operating rules belonging to Session 3, then words each under canon's voice rules.

Two constraints Session 2 recommends: version one is marked pre-opening and drawn from decisions rather than moments, because Sŏn has decisions and no operating history; and every principle passes canon's six binary tests, which rules out the virtue register Stripe uses and forces the statement of what the company does or refuses.

Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in sections 6.2, 6.3, and 6.4 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Founder decision: The mission sentence, the entity it belongs to, and whether it names the cuisine
text_content:
The operating charter needs a mission that no other organization could hold, that is never fully achieved, that does not assert the unproven, and that describes the company rather than the restaurant alone.

Three parts, all Brandon's:

The sentence. The record's nearest candidate, "Most restaurants are pointed at the plate. We are pointed at the relationship. The plate is how we earn the right to have one" (canon 09), is register copy written as a voice example. Tested against her own criterion it fails: other hospitality companies make the relationship-over-product claim.
The entity. The canon header names Future Nostalgia Hospitality Group. The white paper says the parent "stays in the background" and "Sŏn is the only brand the customer meets at the building" (WP p. 36). Her test says the parent and the restaurant cannot share one mission. The white paper also holds that "The restaurant is the proof of concept. The connective layer is the asset" (WP p. 34), which argues the charter is the company's.
The cuisine. Whether Korean food is in the company's mission or lives only in Sŏn's daypart charters.

Session 2 did not write a mission and did not mark one draft. It set out the tests, quoted every candidate in the record, and tested each honestly.

name: Founder decision: Settle ownership of the OS surface between the two seated founders
text_content:
The white paper assigns Brandon "the concept, the operating systems, and the experience" (WP p. 03) and Dominic "the capital, the financial architecture, and the technology build" plus "the data architecture" (WP pp. 03, 05). It then describes the stack's proprietary layer as "the OS surface and the agent layer" (WP p. 22). No founder is named as its owner, and the two stated domains land on the same object.

This is the boundary the founder job description carryover (86ajgnhp7) exists to prevent: a CEO and a CFO/CTO quietly both owning the same thing until it breaks under load.

Options: Brandon owns the specification (what the surface must do, what the agents decide, what a lead sees) and Dominic owns the build and operation, with a stated request path for anything outside the specification; or one seat owns it outright.

Requires both founders. Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in section 7 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Founder decision: Adopt or decline "the order is the decision" as an operating tiebreaker
text_content:
The brand deck (p. 04) and the white paper both state that the company protects bandwidth, then joy, then retention, then results. The deck adds a sentence the text canon does not carry: "the order is the decision."

Adopted into the operating charter, that converts a sequence into a rule with real consequences on a real night: covers are reduced rather than the floor thinned, and a service period that consumes the team's bandwidth is restructured before it is defended on results. The white paper's own framing supports the strong reading ("This is mechanical, not aspirational," WP p. 17).

The decision is whether to accept those consequences as a binding tiebreaker or to hold the sequence as a description of how health works.

Brandon, with Dominic. Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in section 4 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Founder decision: Rule on the six-tier authority hierarchy and the placement of the company non-negotiables
text_content:
The two brand canon artifacts state different six-tier hierarchies. sources/brand-guidelines.md (Version 1.0) ranks: 1 cultural frameworks, 2 positioning and playground philosophy, 3 Jeong and Nunchi, 4 brand architecture, 5 voice and tone, 6 personas. The brand deck (Version 3.0, pp. 32 and 93) ranks: 1 cultural frameworks, 2 company non-negotiables, 3 positioning and philosophy, 4 architecture and identity, 5 executional systems, 6 personas.

The deck gives the company non-negotiables (no exploitation, no toxicity, no disposable people; employee-first) override authority over positioning, architecture, and every executional system. The text canon does not rank them at all. Both artifacts declare themselves closed and governing, and the deck's own rule is that a living document "changes by versioned decision, never by drift."

Three rulings are available: adopt the deck; adopt the text canon and move the non-negotiables into the operating charter; or make the non-negotiables the charter's top tier with canon operating beneath them. The ruling decides whether "no disposable people" outranks a brand or service decision or merely sits beside it.

Brandon rules. Dominic should see it. Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in section 4 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Document: Build the founder knowledge-transfer register
text_content:
Type: Document

The record's founding claim is a company built so it does not depend on either founder's memory. Prompt B of each founder's working-with-me document asks them to list what they know that the house depends on and that is not yet written anywhere the house can read it, with a date for each item. The three lists are consolidated into one register: what is still in a founder's head, what breaks if they are unreachable, and when it moves into the system. The register is reviewed at the founder cadence and closed item by item before opening. It is the audit of how far the founding claim is currently true.

name: Founder decision: Reconcile the two accounts of the chef seat
text_content:
Type: Founder decision

The record holds two statements of the culinary seat that are not the same. The white paper makes the chef partner an equal founding partner who owns the culinary vision. The brand canon, in its held items pending an executive chef hire, states that the brand owns the culinary identity and the chef executes within it. These were written at different times. The chef partner's own reading is invited in their working-with-me document once seated, and the position itself is a three-partner decision. Session 2 carries a carryover on this.

name: Founder decision: Decide who carries the concept's voice to the team
text_content:
Type: Founder decision

The record makes one founder the public voice externally and puts mission and values before mechanics in onboarding, but does not say which founder speaks the concept to the team internally at a rhythm, or whether the two leads carry that voice when the founders are not in the building. A house built to run without its founders implies the leads must be able to. The founders decide which of them holds the internal voice and how it is handed to the leads. Session 2's founder job descriptions depend on the answer.

name: Founder decision: Set the founder decision-rights rule
text_content:
Type: Founder decision

The record holds that authority lives in the domain and that each founder owns their domain outright. It holds exactly one rule for a decision that crosses domains: whether lunch is ever built is an equal decision among all three partners. There is no general rule for which decisions are domain-owned, which are joint, what happens when a domain decision has consequences in another domain (a stack choice that changes the floor; a service decision that changes labor), or how a deadlock among three equal partners resolves. Each founder drafts their own version from inside their domain in prompt D of their working-with-me document; the three of them set the rule together. Session 2 (founding documents) and Session 3 (accountability) need the rule and carry a carryover for it.

name: Founder decision: Ratify the management and leadership position
text_content:
Type: Founder decision

The standard distinction between leadership (direction, change, adaptive problems) and management (execution, stability, technical problems) does not map onto Sŏn's two parallel co-leads, who each carry both modes across a what/how split. The Session 1 page recommends that Sŏn not overlay the distinction on the leads as a second axis, and instead adopt it as a triage rule on problems (does this have a fix, or does it need a judgment?), hold direction at the center as the written vision the leads serve, and treat stability as a property of the system rather than something a lead produces by hand. The founders ratify or amend.

name: Founder decision: Ratify the metronome position
text_content:
Type: Founder decision

Standard scaling advice says to set the pace faster than is comfortable. Sŏn's record sets service tempo by attunement and the daypart's register, never by a clock; sets the build sequence (which daypart opens when, whether lunch exists) by proof, deliberately slowly; and runs the build work itself fast, by multiplication and the stack rather than by founder effort. The Session 1 page argues these as two metronomes, with the build metronome split into a fast tempo and a gated sequence, and names the hazard that the build habit of speed leaks into the room during the first quarter of dinner service. The founders ratify or amend the position. Sessions 4 and 10 inherit it.

name: Founder decision: Ratify the six founder operating principles
text_content:
Type: Founder decision

Sŏn's record (the white paper and the brand canon) holds the material for a set of principles governing how its founders operate, but does not state them as principles. Six have been derived and argued on the Session 1 page of the Operating System doc: the house runs without its founders; employees are the users and the founder's cognition is not the default; name what is open; blame the process, and the founders' processes first; authority lives in the domain, founders included; bandwidth before results, founders included. Each is marked recommended and cites the record it rests on. The founders ratify, amend, or reject each one. Until ratified, later sessions treat them as recommended, not settled.

name: S3: Ch2, The operating system
text_content:
Pages 84 to 134. Chapter 2, The operating system. The longest single section in the book at 81,000 characters.

Sŏn output (draft): planning architecture and decision rights. Who decides what, on what information, at what altitude.

The hard part: her operating system is written for a hierarchical knowledge-work org. Brandon's stated organizational thesis is code-bearing, not load-bearing: the system asks what it knows and how that knowledge moves, rather than who holds authority over whom. These are not the same model. This session either reconciles them or names the departure explicitly. Do not paper over the difference.

Completed 2026-09-11

Deliverable: page 2ky45bmy-31693 in the Sŏn Operating System doc, fifteen sections. Verified against the local source by diff: 599 lines on both sides, headings identical, seventy-two positions on each side, no duplication, correct boundaries. Seventy-two marks: forty-nine recommended, fifteen founder-gated, three chef-gated, five team-filled. Nothing landed, nothing final.

The hard part, answered rather than papered over. Section 3 names her five structural assumptions (a company-division-team-individual cascade; goals replicating down it; a manager above each person who assigns, reviews, and escalates; a leadership team allocating between internal claimants; communications pushed down a hierarchy), tests each against the record's web, and places all forty-seven of her mechanisms in one of three categories: survives intact, survives with its justification replaced, or does not survive. The departure is stated in one sentence: at Sŏn the unit that holds the information sets the goal, holds the metric, and owns the decision inside a pre-stated range; the center integrates and names the commitments; nothing is assigned, reviewed, or escalated by a person standing above another person. Two caveats are kept honest on the page: Sŏn is not self-managed, since authority is real and located in the domain, and what is absent is altitude rather than authority; and the web is a claim about a building that has not opened, which is what section 12 exists to test.

Decision rights, built from Sŏn's own record rather than imported. The rule in three parts: closest competent owner, range stated in advance, escalation triggers named before the event with a destination. Three operating rules attach: a trigger names its destination and "escalate" is not one; a range states what the owner may not do as well as what they may; ranges are set one level out from the position that holds them. The record's eight existing instances are quoted and rewritten into the form, five of them marked incomplete on a named part. Five classes the register does not yet cover are named with rules: decisions reserved to all partners, cross-domain consequence, lead-to-lead disagreement, emergency and closure, and stack changes. The interim two-partner case is argued to the founder ceiling and marked founder-gated.

text_content:
Book pages 70 to 83. Chapter 2, Founding documents. Workbook pp. 11 to 22: Stripe's Operating Principles as a worked example, and the Team Charter template.

Who supplies what, this session

This is a heavily-Brandon session. Read carryover 86ajgnpef before anything else. It governs.

Sŏn's mission, vision, and operating principles are decisions Brandon makes. They are not a synthesis of existing brand language, however elegant that synthesis would be.

The trap, named. Sŏn has a large body of stated material: brand canon (sources/brand-guidelines.md and sources/brand-guidelines-deck.pdf, held locally), the playground philosophy, code-bearing not load-bearing, and the three Korean frameworks. A Claude in this session can assemble a completely plausible Sŏn mission out of those fragments and write it down as settled. That is the failure. Brand canon is an input. It is not a substitute for the decision.

What Claude does here: structure the question. Show what a founding document has to do and what it breaks if it is wrong. Surface every place Sŏn already has an implicit answer and make the implicit explicit so Brandon can accept or reject it deliberately. Argue. Push. Refuse to let a phrase that sounds good pass as a decision.

What Claude does not do: write Sŏn's mission and mark it draft.

Propose freely. Record nothing as decided that Brandon has not said.

Sŏn output

The Sŏn operating charter, specification and structure, with every decision either supplied by Brandon in-session or logged as open. Instrument production is gated on 86ajgn2z5.

The distinction that must hold

Brand canon governs how Sŏn speaks, looks, and positions. The operating charter governs how the company runs, decides, and holds itself accountable. Two artifacts, two jobs. Do not let the charter drift into brand language. Do not let it contradict canon.

Inherited from S1, non-negotiable reads

Sŏn does not scale to 7,000 (86ajgnh8n). Her founding documents are written for a company that will inflate around them. Sŏn opens near full size and stays there. A charter written to organize growth is the wrong charter.

Founder job descriptions do not exist, for either founder. S1 identified this as an input to the operating agreement and the boundary that keeps a CEO and a CFO/CTO from quietly both owning the same thing until it breaks. It belongs in this session.

Compensation philosophy does not exist. S1 called it the largest live gap: Sŏn has a structure, not a philosophy. Decide here whether the philosophy belongs in the charter or waits for S13.

Filed by the Session 1 rerun, 2026-09-11

The record holds two accounts of the chef seat (86akh2qnt), with a founder decision at 86akh2qrp. The founder decision-rights rule does not exist (86akh2qt2), with a founder decision at 86akh2qht.

Two source corrections. Brand canon is the local files, not the archived ClickUp doc. The three profiles in profiles/ predate the allowlist; until 86akh2r4k lands, a session loading a profile applies the override in the context ledger.

Completed 2026-09-11

Deliverable: page 2ky45bmy-31673 in the Sŏn Operating System doc. Thirteen sections: what she asks for, the reframe for a house that does not inflate, the standing problem between canon and charter, the authority hierarchy conflict, the operating charter specification section by section, mission and long-term commitments and principles structured as decisions, the founding seat descriptions, founder decision rights, the chef seat, compensation philosophy, team charters, instrument specifications, and open questions routed. Thirty-three marks: eighteen recommended, twelve founder-gated, two chef-gated, one team-filled. Nothing landed, nothing final.

On the founding documents themselves. No mission, no long-term commitment, and no principle was written. Each was structured: what the instrument has to do, what makes one wrong, every candidate the record already holds quoted and tested against her own criteria, and exactly what Brandon supplies. Where a candidate reading was available it was named as a candidate, its source quoted, and what accepting it would commit Sŏn to stated. None was recorded as a draft. The canon's nearest mission-shaped sentence was tested and fails her uniqueness test.

Three conflicts found inside the record itself.

Canon claims authority the charter would contradict. The deck's cover reads "the source of truth for every decision made under this name"; the canon preamble says the tier hierarchy "governs all decisions." Both hold a rule for canon against a habit and canon against itself. Neither holds a rule for canon against another founding document. The clean split this brief assumed is not one canon agrees to.
The two canon artifacts state different six-tier hierarchies. brand-guidelines.md is Version 1.0; the deck is Version 3.0. The deck ranks the company non-negotiables at tier 2 with override authority over positioning, architecture, and every executional system, and adds "the order is the decision." The text version does not rank them at all. For a charter this decides whether "no disposable people" outranks a brand or service decision. Filed at 86akh3rx4 and 86akh3t00.
The chef seat conflict is about standing, not only ownership. The white paper's "chef partner" is an equal founding partner with a vote on whether a service period is built. Canon's "Executive Chef" is a hire gated by criteria the brand sets. A hiring criterion cannot be applied to a founding partner on the same terms. Extends 86akh2qrp at 86akh3tw9.

Two findings that reframed existing carryovers. The record assigns decision rights at least eight times without ever stating the rule, and the eight share one shape: closest competent owner, pre-stated range, escalation triggers named before the event. That pattern is recommended as the rule; the deadlock case stays founder-gated, sharpened with the interim two-partner case at 86akh3ty7. And the founder job descriptions have a concrete overlap already in the record: Brandon owns "the operating systems," Dominic owns "the technology build" and "the data architecture," and nobody owns the OS surface. Filed at 86akh3t27.

Resolved by the team. The compensation split: founding commitments in the charter because every hiring session needs them to score against, architecture in S13. Team charters: Sŏn deliberately does not use them at her unit, and uses a daypart charter instead, which is also the form the lunch decision takes.

Filed: eighteen typed work items under 86akh1hdg (eight founder decisions, three documents, two processes, two structures, three instruments, all three gated on 86ajgn2z5). Twelve carryovers in the register, linked to S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S12, S13, S16, and S17.

Left open, not closed here. Who carries the concept's voice to the team internally (86akh2qq0). The brief routed it to S2 and S2 did not close it. It now sits against the founding seat description work, since the record makes Brandon "the public voice" without saying who carries the voice inward.

Two record-integrity problems flagged. Both canon artifacts name the archived, excluded ClickUp doc 2ky45bmy-15773 as their record of truth, and the text canon says the Surface-and-Zone Baseline Document lives there, so a canon-referenced governing document is unreachable (86akh3tp5). The white paper names Airtable as its data-layer hub, and Airtable is no longer in use. Both feed the recommended charter design rule: commitments and owners, never tools or addresses.

A correction to this brief. It attributed "life share, not market share" and "the building is not the asset, the customer is" to the record. Neither is verbatim in the white paper. The record's claim is "The restaurant is the proof of concept. The connective layer is the asset" (WP p.34). Brand facts are not asserted from memory, and that applies to briefs as well as to output.

Surface every place Sŏn already has an implicit answer and make the implicit explicit so Brandon can accept or reject it deliberately. Argue. Push. Refuse to let a phrase that sounds good pass as a decision.

**What Claude does not do:** write Sŏn's mission and mark it draft.

**Propose freely. Record nothing as decided that Brandon has not said.**

## Sŏn output

The Sŏn operating charter, **specification and structure**, with every decision either supplied by Brandon in-session or logged as open. Instrument production is gated on `86ajgn2z5`.

## The distinction that must hold

Brand canon governs how Sŏn speaks, looks, and positions. The operating charter governs how the company runs, decides, and holds itself accountable. Two artifacts, two jobs. Do not let the charter drift into brand language. Do not let it contradict canon.

## Inherited from S1, non-negotiable reads

**Sŏn does not scale to 7,000** (`86ajgnh8n`). Her founding documents are written for a company that will inflate around them. Sŏn opens near full size and stays there. A charter written to organize growth is the wrong charter.

**Founder job descriptions do not exist**, for either founder. S1 identified this as an input to the operating agreement and the boundary that keeps a CEO and a CFO/CTO from quietly both owning the same thing until it breaks. It belongs in this session.

**Compensation philosophy does not exist.** S1 called it the largest live gap: Sŏn has a structure, not a philosophy. Decide here whether the philosophy belongs in the charter or waits for S13.

## Filed by the Session 1 rerun, 2026-09-11

**The record holds two accounts of the chef seat** (`86akh2qnt`), with a founder decision at `86akh2qrp`. **The founder decision-rights rule does not exist** (`86akh2qt2`), with a founder decision at `86akh2qht`.

**Two source corrections.** Brand canon is the local files, not the archived ClickUp doc. The three profiles in `profiles/` predate the allowlist; until `86akh2r4k` lands, a session loading a profile applies the override in the context ledger.

* * *

## Completed 2026-09-11

**Deliverable:** page `2ky45bmy-31673` in the Sŏn Operating System doc. Thirteen sections: what she asks for, the reframe for a house that does not inflate, the standing problem between canon and charter, the authority hierarchy conflict, the operating charter specification section by section, mission and long-term commitments and principles structured as decisions, the founding seat descriptions, founder decision rights, the chef seat, compensation philosophy, team charters, instrument specifications, and open questions routed. Thirty-three marks: eighteen recommended, twelve founder-gated, two chef-gated, one team-filled. Nothing landed, nothing final.

**On the founding documents themselves.** No mission, no long-term commitment, and no principle was written. Each was structured: what the instrument has to do, what makes one wrong, every candidate the record already holds quoted and tested against her own criteria, and exactly what Brandon supplies. Where a candidate reading was available it was named as a candidate, its source quoted, and what accepting it would commit Sŏn to stated. None was recorded as a draft. The canon's nearest mission-shaped sentence was tested and fails her uniqueness test.

**Three conflicts found inside the record itself.**

1. **Canon claims authority the charter would contradict.** The deck's cover reads "the source of truth for every decision made under this name"; the canon preamble says the tier hierarchy "governs all decisions." Both hold a rule for canon against a habit and canon against itself. Neither holds a rule for canon against another founding document. The clean split this brief assumed is not one canon agrees to.
2. **The two canon artifacts state different six-tier hierarchies.** `brand-guidelines.md` is Version 1.0; the deck is Version 3.0. The deck ranks the company non-negotiables at tier 2 with override authority over positioning, architecture, and every executional system, and adds "the order is the decision." The text version does not rank them at all. For a charter this decides whether "no disposable people" outranks a brand or service decision. Filed at `86akh3rx4` and `86akh3t00`.
3. **The chef seat conflict is about standing, not only ownership.** The white paper's "chef partner" is an equal founding partner with a vote on whether a service period is built. Canon's "Executive Chef" is a hire gated by criteria the brand sets. A hiring criterion cannot be applied to a founding partner on the same terms. Extends `86akh2qrp` at `86akh3tw9`.

**Two findings that reframed existing carryovers.** The record assigns decision rights at least eight times without ever stating the rule, and the eight share one shape: closest competent owner, pre-stated range, escalation triggers named before the event. That pattern is recommended as the rule; the deadlock case stays founder-gated, sharpened with the interim two-partner case at `86akh3ty7`. And the founder job descriptions have a concrete overlap already in the record: Brandon owns "the operating systems," Dominic owns "the technology build" and "the data architecture," and nobody owns the OS surface. Filed at `86akh3t27`.

**Resolved by the team.** The compensation split: founding commitments in the charter because every hiring session needs them to score against, architecture in S13. Team charters: Sŏn deliberately does not use them at her unit, and uses a daypart charter instead, which is also the form the lunch decision takes.

**Filed:** eighteen typed work items under `86akh1hdg` (eight founder decisions, three documents, two processes, two structures, three instruments, all three gated on `86ajgn2z5`). Twelve carryovers in the register, linked to S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S12, S13, S16, and S17.

**Left open, not closed here.** Who carries the concept's voice to the team internally (`86akh2qq0`). The brief routed it to S2 and S2 did not close it. It now sits against the founding seat description work, since the record makes Brandon "the public voice" without saying who carries the voice inward.

**Two record-integrity problems flagged.** Both canon artifacts name the archived, excluded ClickUp doc `2ky45bmy-15773` as their record of truth, and the text canon says the Surface-and-Zone Baseline Document lives there, so a canon-referenced governing document is unreachable (`86akh3tp5`). The white paper names Airtable as its data-layer hub, and Airtable is no longer in use. Both feed the recommended charter design rule: commitments and owners, never tools or addresses.

**A correction to this brief.** It attributed "life share, not market share" and "the building is not the asset, the customer is" to the record. Neither is verbatim in the white paper. The record's claim is "The restaurant is the proof of concept. The connective layer is the asset" (WP p.34). Brand facts are not asserted from memory, and that applies to briefs as well as to output.

name: S1: Introduction + Ch1, Essential Operating Principles
text_content:
Book: pages 9 to 69. Introduction, plus Chapter 1: Essential Operating Principles.

Workbook: Chapter 1 section, plus pages ~80 to 85. Two pulls, not one.

Covers: setting your metronome, the core frameworks, build self-awareness to build mutual awareness, say the thing you think you cannot say, management vs leadership, come back to your operating system.

The workbook material this session needs:
Chapter 1: Management Prerequisites Checklist, Understand Your Values (adapted from Stan Slap), work style grid (introvert/extrovert against people/task oriented, producing Analyzer, Director, Collaborator, Promoter), strengths inventory split into innate vs acquired skills and capabilities.
Chapter 3, around pp. 80 to 85: "Working with Claire," her own worked example, and the "Working with Me" template. She files these as onboarding artifacts, not self-awareness ones. Pull them forward. The Chapter 1 exercises are the input, the Chapter 3 template is the container.

Sŏn output (draft):
Founder operating principles
Working-with-me document, Brandon
Working-with-me document, Dominic
Working-with-me template for the incoming chef partner, built as a prompt for that person, not filled in on their behalf

Notes: This feeds the operating agreement work already done with Dominic, and it is a direct input to the chef partner relationship. Chapter 1 is about the manager's self-awareness before it is about anyone else's.

Watch the Management Prerequisites Checklist. It assumes 1:1s, job ladders, levels, and a compensation philosophy. Sŏn has none of those yet and its compensation is embedded revenue share. Read it as a gap list, not a scorecard.

Completed 2026-09-11 (rerun)

Deliverable: page 2ky45bmy-31653 in the Sŏn Operating System doc. Eight sections: the six founder operating principles, the metronome, management and leadership, come back to your operating system, the prerequisites read as a gap list, the working-with-me document, the working-with-me template in full, and five instrument specifications. Thirty-three marks: nineteen recommended, ten founder-gated, three chef-gated, two team-filled. Nothing landed, nothing final.

On the working-with-me outputs. The brief named filled documents for Brandon and Dominic. Those were not written, because the team does not generate a founder's interiority and the first pass was un-made partly for reaching there. What the session produced instead, on Brandon's instruction, is the complete template content: one spine of eleven prompts, each with what it asks, what it is really asking for, how to answer well, and what a weak answer looks like, plus three seat-specific preambles and three prerequisite self-exercises. Each founder completes their own. The chef partner's preamble is written as a prompt to that person and nothing is filled in on their behalf. The formatted fillable artifact is gated on the document methodology 86ajgn2z5 and is filed separately.

Filed: twelve typed work items under 86akh1hdg (six founder decisions, four documents, one instrument, one structure). Five carryovers in the register, linked to S2, S3, S4, S8, and S16.

Left open on purpose: when the working-with-me document is exchanged with the chef partner, which routes to S7 (86ajgnj8t). The first pass closed this without standing and the closure was un-made. This session did not close it either.

Two conflicts found inside the record itself, not between the book and Sŏn: the white paper and the brand canon disagree about who owns culinary identity (86akh2qnt), and they name the room-owning role differently (86akh2r3e). Both surfaced only because the white paper was read in full.

Three instances of pre-allowlist drift corrected or flagged: the Operating System index still described pages as draft or final (corrected); the S2 brief pointed at the archived ClickUp canon doc (corrected); the three profiles cite the V7 notebook, route figures to Airtable, and use the retired mark "landed" (override recorded in the ledger, rewrite filed at 86akh2r4k).

name: Scaling People: translation program
text_content:
Program

Translate Claire Hughes Johnson's Scaling People into Sŏn's operating structure and systems, chapter by chapter. The book is a guide, upstream of Sŏn's own thinking, not foreign material to translate.

The tracker doc is the single source of truth for how this program runs: 2ky45bmy-17233. Read its protocol block before every session. This task description is a pointer, not a duplicate, so the two cannot drift.

The one-line frame

Her ask → what Sŏn already holds (from V7 and canon) → the gap → the decision.

The team

Three profiles, live in Box, folder 400727361228. Loaded by chapter ownership, not all at once.
Organizational Systems Architect (2352980282301): her Ch1, Ch2, the progression structure.
People Systems Designer (2353165009738): her Ch3, Ch4, Ch5.
Hospitality Operations Realist (2353380918688): cross-cutting tempo test.

Cold-start

New chat, attach both PDFs (book + workbook), paste:

Sŏn. Scaling People, session [N]. ClickUp task [ID]. Begin.

The session reads its brief, its carryovers, the context ledger, the profiles its chapter needs, and the named V7 and canon sections, then works. Full sequence and the definition of done are in the tracker protocol.

What sessions produce

Decisions and specifications, written to the Sŏn Operating System doc (2ky45bmy-17253). Never instruments; instrument production is gated on the document methodology (86ajgn2z5).

The four protocols that make this survivable over weeks

All detailed in the tracker:
Context ledger: a short running-state section read at the start of every session and updated at the end. The anti-drift mechanism across 20+ sessions. The chat is disposable; the ledger is the memory.
Tangent protocol: when a non-linear thread surfaces, the session names it (carryover / pull now with a park / research now-or-later), recommends, and Brandon decides. Nothing held loose in a chat.
Pause and resume: "pausing here" writes state to the ledger, files loose thoughts as carryovers, and confirms the next action. Resuming reads the ledger, never the chat.
Token discipline: load by ownership, read by page range, carry state in the ledger not the chat, one session per chat.

Standing rules

Customer never guest. No em dashes. No performed conviction. Declarative over aspirational. Sentence case. No daypart code names. No financial figures; from Airtable (appKHeje63inr1fLG) or absent. Profanity spoken-only.

From the June 29, 2026 meeting transcript: this is a narrative task, not a working MVP build.

Goal: explain the Sun Technology Operating System in plain investor-facing language: what it does, why it matters, and why Brandon + Dominic are the right team to execute it.

Current framing:

MVP = mapped-out plan MVP, not working software yet.
Show value through operational bandwidth: DMs, invoices/AP, reservations, repetitive ops, social/customer response, training modules, and business admin that becomes less manual.
Show business intelligence advantage: data and operating visibility traditional restaurants do not have.

name: Pull The Josephine from all investor materials (white papers, deck, live site)
text_content:
Decision: The Josephine comes out of all investor-facing materials. Locke (their CEO) has gone largely unresponsive and trust has eroded. We remain open to running it, but it cannot be cited as proof or traction until that changes, so it is pulled from materials now.

What this removes: The Josephine was the only demand-proof / operational-record element in the raise argument, and it was already the soft link (no executed events, realized revenue, or completed compliance). With it pulled, the materials stand on the operator, the market, and the model. That is honest for a teaser site. Real, citable proof returns to the deck and data room only when it exists.

Scope (where it appears):

Investor website prompt (v2): Room 6 / Proof removed, Request renumbered to 06. DONE.
White papers in Box folder 382453064958 (5 files). The Gladwell paper's "Why this, why here, why now" section names the San Antonio pop-up explicitly ("building a book of business now... demand gets demonstrated before the doors open"). All five need the San Antonio / Josephine proof claim removed and the surrounding argument re-footed so it does not lean on demonstrated demand.
Pitch deck: any proof / traction slide or mention.
Live site (sonrestaurant.com): the Invest page frames The Josephine as a live operating program ("the demand is not a projection"). Remove on the same pass that addresses the other live-site issues.

Do not touch: the Josephine venture's own ClickUp space and Airtable base stay as-is. This is a materials change, not a venture shutdown.

Status: to do. Website prompt done. White papers, deck, live site pending.

text_content:
Flagged by Brandon during the investor-website rebuild (this session).

Decision to implement: Split the site's copy by register.

Vee (conviction) voice writes all non-narrative copy: the short, high-impact statements, eyebrows, section claims, the "capture" lines, CTAs. Conviction and momentum, compressed.
Gladwell (narrative) voice writes the single narrative element. Brandon strongly favors the Gladwell narrative version already produced; open question is where it lives on the site so it lands without breaking the funnel.
House voice remains the orchestrator that braids the two inside one surface.

Hard constraints these voices must obey (Brand Guidelines §09 + global voice rule):

No exclamation points and no emoji in any written brand voice. Vee's energy comes through compression and certainty, not punctuation.
Profanity is spoken-only. Never in written output, in any voice, absent an explicit per-piece override.
Sentence case; UPPERCASE only for one-line eyebrows.
Forbidden lexicon is absolute (incl. memorable, elevated, experiential, seasonal, journey, "we believe," performed conviction).
Longer-form digital prohibits founder-story-as-hero-narrative and revelation-arc. The Gladwell placement must thread this, not violate it.

Dependency: The full brand narrative is canonically held pending the Executive Chef hire (Brand Guidelines §01 and §09 "Open"), and the prototype's "Founder's deeper why" is a held placeholder set by Brandon's own material. What ships now is a constrained narrative, not the full version.

Status: decision captured; execution happens when site copy is written (after IA + design direction lock).

Status: CLOSED
